children: Egypt has drawn up plans to invest nearly $10 billion in petrochemical projects to expand output and nearly triple revenues from such products.
The state-owned Egyptian Petrochemicals Holding company (Echem) said it would pump the new investments during the 2026-2030 development plan.

The plan covers eight new projects targeting 20 products with a total output capacity of 6.5 million tonnes per year, its chairman Alauddin Abdel Fattah said during a board meeting headed by petroleum and mineral resources minister Karim Badawi.
“We are targeting annual production of 6.5 million tonnes per year, with expected revenues of nearly $7 billion,” Abdel Fattah said after Friday’s meeting.

His figures showed Echem already achieved record production of 4.6 million tonnes during the 2025-2026 fiscal year, with revenues standing at $2.6 billion, including around $1.8 billion generated from exports to nearly 50 countries.
Key markets included Asia, Europe and the Arab region besides new markets such as Cyprus, Romania, Slovenia and Brazil, Abdel Fattah said.
Egypt has been encouraged by a rebound in oil and gas production over the past year to embark on plans to expand its oil-related industries, including refining.

In September last year, the petroleum and mineral resources ministry said that Egypt’s gas production has started to decline at a slower rate and is expected to recover following significant discoveries by global companies operating in the Arab country.

Badawi said in late 2025 that bp and other global oil giants have devised multi-billion- dollar investment plans for the next five years to develop Egypt’s gas wealth and reverse a three-year decline in its production.
Badawi also unveiled a five-year plan to invest nearly $5.7 billion in oil operations, involving the drilling of 480 oil wells
(Writing by N Saeed; Editing by Anoop Menon)
